what: Handset photograph of the boot log overlaid on the UniXNU menu screen, taken during one boot that did not move past the hand-off
captured: 2026-11-27 (Asia/Shanghai), supplied by the device owner; the owner corrected this session's first reading
corrections: The earlier reading of this photograph -- 'the device returned to the menu after the hand-off' -- was wrong, and the device owner said so: the device did not go back to the menu. The menu text ('Booting iOS 16.7.16 in 1 s', the key help, 'drivers 2 loaded / 0 failed') is the menu screen that was already drawn, and the boot log lines are printed over it without clearing the panel.
So this is the same single boot as the hand-off photograph, not a second one: menu drawn, then DarwinBoot's log and the hand-off page printed on top, and nothing after that.

observations.menu_text: UniXNU 0.1.0, config \EFI\UniXNU\unixnu.toml, entry 1 'iOS 16.7.16' (xnu), 'Booting iOS 16.7.16 in 1 s'
observations.menu_footer: Up/Down: select   Enter: boot   1-9: boot entry   Esc: stop timer   drivers 2 loaded / 0 failed   kits 0   acpi 0
observations.boot_log: DARWINBOOT lines and the hand-off page printed over the menu, exactly as in the hand-off photograph
observations.loader_bar: green bar at the top of the screen
observations.device_state: the screen stayed on this page; the device did not return to the menu and did not visibly reset

reading: The chain runs to the branch to XNU and then the handset shows nothing further, on a screen that stays put rather than restarting -- the shell of the failure is a hang or a quiet fault, not a reset loop.
A kernel that faults into its own early vectors before the console mapping exists has no way to print, which matches this picture exactly; a kernel that hangs in early setup would look the same.
